look_here_first: Think tall, glaucous perennial with highly dissected fingerlike leaves and NO involucellar bractlets. The inflorescence is paniculate, stipules are usually shed early, and the calyx lobes meet into a pointed bud.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial from thickened root, usually erect rather than trailing

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems glaucous and nearly glabrous, commonly 0.5–2 m in FNA

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves deeply 5–10-lobed with very narrow linear to lanceolate ultimate segments

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stipules caducous, often absent by flowering

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx lobes valvate in bud and form an apiculate/acuminate point

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers reddish-purple, but color is not diagnostic

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mericarps glabrous and indehiscent, beaks not prominent

lookalikes.differences: Callirhoe pedata: C. pedata is Texas-native, usually has persistent stipules and a racemose inflorescence; its leaves are 3–5-lobed rather than typically 5–10-lobed, though both can be strongly dissected. Callirhoe leiocarpa: C. leiocarpa is annual/biennial, with dehiscent mericarps and prominent beaks/collars; C. digitata is perennial with indehiscent fruit. Callirhoe involucrata: Winecup has 3 involucellar bractlets and a low trailing habit; C. digitata lacks the involucel and is tall/erect.
